COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
23.09.2025 In Re: Protecting Dignity of Woman Suo Motu PIL No.186 of 2025
Hon'ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel brings to 
the notice of this Court some disturbing 
developments wherein certain posts made on 
Twitter and Facebook in respect of a ruling 
rendered by the Hon’ble Apex Court where the 
accused came to be acquitted by a judgment of the 
Hon’ble Apex Court.
4. The posts are not merely vituperative 
intimidating and provocatory but, in fact, braying 
for the blood of the counsel, who rendered her 
professional duties.
5. It is most unfortunate that the social media 
platforms are a remit for the immature, the 
unreasonable and oral incontinence and is turning 
into a nasty circus. In fact, one post reads “give 
betel nut to known people for such individuals” 
probably referring to the word “supari” which is the 
native term used for betel nut, and thereby  implying ‘a contract to kill’ be given.
6. Some of the posts are so provocative and only 
god knows what an imbalanced mind would do 
after reading such posts.
7. We are at a loss to understand as to how the 
social media platforms are hosting such posts and 
without accountability.
8. The DGP and the IG (Head of Cyber Crimes) 
to virtually appear before this Court during the 
course of the day.
9. We request the Deputy Advocate General to 
forthwith inform the same to the concerned 
officers.
10. The Senior Superintendent of Police, Nainital 
shall forthwith provide all security to petitioner and 
the concerned family members.
11. Registrar (Judicial) to communicate this order 
to Senior Superintendent of Police, Nainital.
12. No congregations or protests shall be allowed 
near the office premises and residence of the 
learned counsels.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.)
 23.09.2025 23.09.2025
KK/SS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
23.09.2025 In Re: Suo Motu PIL No. Nil of 2025
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J. 
1. Heard the Inspector General of Police 
(Cyber Crimes).
2. The IG (Cyber Crimes) expresses his
shock with the content of the posts.
3. In fact, one message clearly amounts to 
giving provocation to anybody to engage a 
hired killer. The other posts are utterly 
distasteful and are directly demeaning of the 
judgment of the Hon’ble Apex Court. What is 
ever more shocking is the social media 
platforms hosting and retaining such 
provocative, intimidative and most vituperative
content. One post states that the counsel who 
defended the accused and her family members 
should also be visited with the same action. 
The post are of such nature that immature 
minds will certainly get influenced by them and 
will heighten emotions in the society and breed
a sense of vengeance and enmity against the 
targeted persons.  4. One post says “shoot this one too, and 
along with it, ……., as well”. One post 
describes the judgment as ‘a joke’.
5. We direct the IG (Cyber Crimes) to 
forthwith initiate proceedings and direct the 
social media platforms to pull down such 
posts. 
6. The Registry is directed to register this as 
a Suo Motu PIL. 
7. Social media platforms like X, You Tube, 
Facebook, Instagram etc. be arrayed as party 
respondents.
8. We appoint the Deputy Advocate General 
for the State, Mr. J.S. Virk, as Amicus Curiae
to assist the Court.
9. List on 25.09.2025, at 04:00 P.M.
10. The IG (Cyber Crimes) and the SSP, 
Nainital to submit an action taken note by 
then.
 
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.)
 23.09.2025 23.09.2025
Negi

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
25.09.2025 WPPIL No. 186 of 2025
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Amicus Curiae.
2. In compliance with our earlier order dated 
23.09.2025, the SSP, Nainital and the IG, Cyber 
Crimes are present before the Court. The SSP has filed 
into the Court the Action Taken Report. 
3. Learned DAG submits that, in compliance of the 
directions issued by this Court, two Personal Security 
Officers have been assigned for the protection of the 
person (whom we would designate as victim for the 
sake of the proceedings). The IG, Cyber Crimes has 
submitted a compliance report, wherein it is stated that 
03 primary posts have been identified, and that the 
said 03 posts have been re-tweeted multiple times, and 
are being widely shared; and that they are registered 
with Ticket Nos. LD-17194, LD-17197 & LD-17198; and 
that they have also identified 10 other objectionable 
comments; and that orders of this Court have also 
been forwarded to the social media platforms like 
Twitter/X, and that SSP STF, namely Navneet Singh & 
DySP Cyber, namely Ankush Mishra have also got in 
touch with the designated representatives of Twitter/X,
and the contact number is also provided; the 
instructions to pull down the posts have also been 
conveyed through phone calls and WhatsApp; and that 
the representative has acknowledge the receipt of the 
notices, and has also informed that the matter has 
been escalated to the parent company in the USA for 
necessary compliance; and that the compliance from 
the end of the social media platforms is awaited. The  compliance report is taken on record. 
4. We hope that the social media platforms i.e. 
WhatsApp, Meta, Facebook, Twitter/X would abide by 
the directions, with the necessary urgency that the 
matter requires. The dignity of women, by itself, and 
in the context of our culture, is absolutely non￾negotiable. We hope that the spirit, with which this 
order is made, and the legal compulsions are 
considered in right earnest, and action initiated with 
speed. 
5. Copy of this order be forwarded to the IG, Cyber 
Crimes. 
6. Registry to print the name of Mr. J.S. Virk, 
Advocate as learned Amicus Curiae.
7. List this case on 17.10.2025.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 25.09.2025 25.09.2025
Rahul

Hon’ble G. Narendar, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Amicus Curiae for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Rakesh Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State 
of Uttarakhand.
3. Heard the learned Amicus Curiae Shri J.S. Virk.
4. Learned counsel Shri Karthik Jayashankar submits 
that he is instructed to appear on behalf of the proposed 
6th respondent M/s X Corporation.
5. The submission is placed on record.
6. Learned Amicus Curiae has preferred an application 
for impleading certain social media platforms, namely, M/s 
Meta Platform, X Corporation, WhatsApp Application 
Services Private Ltd. and Facebook India Online Services 
Private Limited. 
7. In the light of the submissions made by learned 
Counsel Shri Jayashankar, the X Corporation is directed to 
be arrayed as respondent no.5.
8. Issue notices to the proposed respondents M/s Meta 
Platform Inc. Instagram Designated Agent, M/s Whatsapp 
Application Services Private Ltd., Salarpuria and Facebook 
India Online Services Private Limited.
9. We have queried Mr. Jayashankar as to whether  technology used by M/s X Corporation enables red￾flagging messages, which carry un-parliamentary, vulgar 
and provocative words. We have also queried as to 
whether M/s X Corporation has any mechanism to pull 
down such messages on its own accord and thirdly, 
whether the social media platforms ought to be made 
liable to compensate the victims of such online onslaughts.
10. The learned counsel Shri Jayashankar submits that 
he would secure instructions in this regard and prays for 
two weeks’ time.
11. Learned Amicus Curiae files a communication from 
the DGP whereby the investigation into the offences
complained of have been handed over to the SSP, STF 
Dehradun.
12. We direct the Amicus Curiae to array SSP, STF 
Dehradun as a party respondent.
13. Learned counsel Shri Jaishankar has also placed 
before the Court a note stating that two of the posts have 
been deleted by the user and one post has been withheld
by X. It is further stated that the details of the account 
holders have also been shared with the respondent police.
14. The SSP, STF, Dehradun is also permitted to 
communicate to the proposed respondents regarding the 
pendency of the petition and the next date of hearing.
15. List this case on 24.11.2025.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.)

Senior Counsel Shri Vivek Reddy for respondent no.7.

submit that respondent no.8 (Facebook) is not a 
necessary party as it does not run a social media 
platform and similarly the learned senior counsel Shri 
Vivek Reddy would submit that WhatsApp LLC. is the 
appropriate party and hence the array of parties needs to  be looked in and corrected. The submissions are placed 
on record.
7. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents 
may communicate with the learned Amicus Curiae and 
convey the correct position. The learned Amicus Curiae is 
requested to look into the same and file appropriate 
applications either to implead the necessary parties or to

request two weeks’ time to file a statement.

to whether any mechanism can be developed by the 
social media entities to ensure that certain obnoxious/ 
descriptive, un-parliamentary, vulgar, abusive or 
demeaning words can be automatically/voluntarily

and secondly to ensure/enable a mechanism which would 
prevent re-tweeting or reposting of such offensive posts.
10. Learned senior counsels would submit that they 
would secure instructions and make appropriate 
submissions before this Court. Same is placed on record. 
11. List on 15.12.2025.
